The 5-2 Browns visit the 5-2 Steelers for an AFC North rivalry at Acrisure Stadium, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

setup: Cleveland and Pittsburgh renew their AFC North rivalry with matching 5–2 records, and the rematch comes a month after the Browns' 27–24 win on October 1. This time the Steelers have the home field and a chance to answer the earlier result.

The Browns bring Deshaun Watson's improving passing production and a hard-running Quinshon Judkins, while Pittsburgh leans on Aaron Rodgers, Jaylen Warren and DK Metcalf. Field position and protection could decide another close divisional contest.

things.title: Rodgers against Cleveland's rush
things.body: Cleveland's front can make even quick-release quarterback Aaron Rodgers uncomfortable. Pittsburgh must avoid long third downs and create safe outlets for its backs and tight ends before pressure arrives.

things.title: Judkins on early downs
things.body: Quinshon Judkins has shown he can finish drives and create tough yards. Cleveland will look to build favorable second downs rather than forcing Watson into constant obvious passing situations.

things.title: Metcalf's big-play threat
things.body: DK Metcalf produced 115 receiving yards in their October meeting, including key second-half gains. Cleveland must limit his explosive receptions while accounting for Pittsburgh's intermediate targets.

paths_to_win.body: Win the line of scrimmage with Judkins, keep Watson clean and pressure Rodgers without allowing a long catch-and-run. Recreating the defensive stops that helped win the first matchup would give Cleveland the edge late.

Balance Warren's touches with quick throws, get Metcalf involved early, and keep turnovers down. If the defense gets Cleveland behind schedule, Pittsburgh can control field position and make its home-field advantage matter.

players.name: Jaylen Warren

players.name: DK Metcalf
players.body: The downfield target already hurt Cleveland in the teams' October game.

unit_edges.title: Cleveland front vs Pittsburgh blockers
unit_edges.body: Cleveland can dictate down-and-distance if its defensive line creates early penetration. Pittsburgh has to protect Rodgers and get Warren into space before the Browns' edge pressure closes in.

unit_edges.title: Pittsburgh front vs Cleveland rushing game
unit_edges.body: Pittsburgh's run fits and linebacker tackling are tested by Judkins. If the Steelers force Watson into longer dropbacks, the defense can attack the passer instead of chasing the run.
